item: new_to_faith — New to faith and returning
angle: Veteran pastor / pastoral counsellor: what the person feels at each moment, the words that land and the words that wound, presence over problem-solving, the human next step.
thesis: Two different people come through this one door — someone who has never opened a Bible, and someone who has been gone a while and does not want to be asked why. The app already gets Day 1 right: one short passage, plain words, one button, questions under the teaching, complete on the same screen. It loses them on Day 2, when the Day N surface stops serving 3-7 verses and starts serving a whole chapter of Paul, and calls the button "Mark Complete" on a journey whose first lesson is that God does not reward performance. The fix is not a new screen and not a smaller app. It is: size the daily unit to what Day 1 already is, put one plain-English meaning under the hard word, name the returning person once without asking why, stop calling reading "complete", and put a hand out on Day 10. Everything Ashley locked — the photo hero, the sage button, the journey-only home, the Superdesign landing, the ruled question placement — stays exactly as it is.
principles: Never ask why they left. 51% of the dechurched think they may return and most left for mundane reasons — moved, inconvenience — not doctrine or scandal (research, Persona 1, Davis & Graham 2023). Practical friction is high; shame is lower than assumed. A question about the past is friction we add ourselves.

The second week is the product, not the first tap. Curiosity is up and conversion is not; the research's own headline is that the problem is the second week (cross-cutting 1). Day 1 is already right. Days 2-14 are where the design work belongs.

One short passage, not a chapter. Newcomer plans work as one thought plus a few verses; YouVersion raised plan completion by front-loading accessible material, and people quit early in hard opening material (Persona 1, Where they quit).

No word on this path may imply performance. The Day 1 lesson says grace "doesn't reward performance — it replaces it", and the button under it currently says Mark Complete. Language has to agree with the teaching.

Progress is the journey, never a streak. Day N of 40 waits for you; a streak punishes you. Guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall (cross-cutting 6). The new_to_faith greeting already never mentions the streak — keep it that way.
Every visible line relates to the one sage button (Ashley, 1 Sep 2026). Anything added to this path must be part of the day's reading or it does not go on Home.
Richer and clearer, never stripped. Additions here are one line, one quiet row, one toggle — inside the locked editorial look, not a rebuild of it.

Presence beats problem-solving. The person new to faith who is also in crisis is the most exposed person in the whole app; comfort must be one tap from the reading without asking them to change who they are.

journey.day0: They land cold on futuresdailyword.com (or a Sunday QR). App.tsx pre-render silently enrols them as new_to_faith/source:'default' and Day1Landing replaces the tab shell. What they feel: 'I don't know what I'm doing' or 'I've been gone a long time'. What they see: wordmark, language switch, 'Day 1 of 40 · New & Returning to Faith', 'Grace Changes Everything', one new line naming both people, one Read button, and the quiet 'Not new to faith? Choose your path' link. No account, no picker, no gate. KEEP ALL OF IT — this screen already does its job.
journey.first_session: Tap Read: the reading opens in place (no navigation, no new screen). Ephesians 2:8-9 on the white paper card, one plain-meaning line under the reference ('Grace: a gift you didn't earn'), three short pastoral paragraphs, Day 1's two Reflect & Respond questions, 'Day 1 of 40', 'Mark as read'. Tapping it stamps the day, advances the journey, records the streak silently, and hands off to the ruled sequence: PathAskedOnce → push ask → later the email card. Total: about four minutes, one decision, nothing asked of them they cannot answer.
journey.return_visit: Day 2 opens straight to the tab shell — no landing, no picker. Home is the journey and nothing else: greeting, the 'how it works' line, the photo hero carrying 'Day 2 of 40', the day's title, the progress bar and one sage Read button. Tapping it opens the full-screen Day N surface. THIS is where today's design does its work: the assigned verses open (2 Corinthians 5:17, not all of 2 Corinthians 5), 'Read the whole chapter' sits under them for the day they want more, the glossary row offers the one hard word, then the teaching, then the two questions, then 'Mark as read'.
journey.week2: Days 8-14 are the doctrinal middle of the journey — Romans 3 on sin, 1 John 1 on repentance, Acts 2 on the Holy Spirit. Longest lessons in the whole 40 (2,540 chars on Day 8). The verse-sized reading matters most here. Day 10 ('Rest — You Don't Have to Earn It', Matthew 11:28-30) carries the one relational move: a single quiet card under the questions offering to have someone from their campus read it with them. Once, dismissible, never a chat, never blocking. By Day 14 they have a 14-day progress bar, answers saved against ten days, and one human who knows they exist.
journey.missed_day: They miss two, four, nine days. Nothing chases them. The streak engine bridges one day with its freeze and otherwise resets quietly; the new_to_faith greeting never surfaces a streak, so there is nothing to lose. On return the journey is exactly where they left it — Day 7 is still Day 7 — and one line acknowledges the gap without counting it: 'Day 7 has been waiting for you.' Never 'you missed 3 days', never a broken-flame graphic, never a catch-up offer. The push reminder names the day, never the streak.
journey.seasonal: Day 40 is the one calendar moment this path has, and today it ends on '✓ Day 40 complete' and silence — a person finishes forty days of finding faith and the app says nothing. Day 40 closes with a named ending and one next step: the congregation path offered through the existing ChoosePathSheet as a real choice (source 'upgrade'). This is NOT comfort's banned 'Feeling Stronger?' graduation prompt — that ruling is scoped to the comfort path, where nothing may ever be asked of the reader; a completion moment at the end of a 40-day journey the person chose is a different object, and it needs Ashley's explicit word before it is built.

comfort_access: One tap, from the reading, without changing who they said they were. The line sits at the foot of the Day N surface — 'Going through something hard right now? Open comfort' — and opens the comfort chapter as an overlay above the journey. It does NOT call saveSetup, so their saved path stays new_to_faith (research: 'crisis is not a persona someone chooses on a good day'); it does NOT route through handleRead, so it credits nothing (same rule class as the ruled credit-free arrival seed); the toolbar is Note + Close only (ruled); and there is no graduation prompt of any kind (ruled, comfort). Closing returns them to the same day, nothing lost. It does NOT go on the I'm-New Home — Ashley's 1 Sep ruling is that every line on that screen relates to the sage journey button, and a comfort card on Home would be the first thing to break it. The same line also belongs on the More tab for every path; that is the cross-cutting build, not this one. Whether it may ALSO appear on Home for this path is an owner decision, listed below. Safety flow (crisis language typed into Bible AI or a prayer request → gentle confirm → region-correct line: 988 US, 13 11 14 AU, 0800 543 354 NZ) is the cross-cutting comfort build and must land there, not be forked here; the research's finding that only 35% of mental-health apps show crisis resources in-app is the reason it cannot wait.
reminders: One a day, named by the day, never by the streak. The push body for this path is 'Day {n} is ready when you are.' and, after a gap of two or more days, 'Day {n} is still here.' — no count of missed days, no flame, no 'don't lose your streak'. Guilt-framed streak reminders are the documented driver of notification opt-out and uninstall (cross-cutting 6), and this is the persona least able to absorb a scolding. The ask itself stays exactly where it is: after the first finished reading, never before, never stacked (ruled). Timing: the cron already sends at each subscriber's stored preferred_hour with a 2-hour catch-up window; the research's behaviour-inferred timing (nudge when they actually open, after 5-7 sessions) is a genuine improvement but it is a push-send.js change that affects every path, so it belongs to the cross-cutting reminders build, not this one. Missed days: the streak engine's single freeze, replenished after 7 days, is the streak-repair mechanic the research asks for and it already exists — leave it alone. Note for anyone touching it: the milestone list is duplicated in two files (streak.ts:14 and GreetingSection.tsx:6) and they disagree; any no-shame change has to touch both or the greeting will celebrate a milestone the engine does not recognise.
instrumentation: FIRST, FIX THE PIPE. track() only writes to Supabase when dw_profile.email exists (src/utils/analytics.ts:69-82) — and this persona has no email until AFTER the first read, the push ask and the email card. The one persona whose D1/D7 we most need is the one the app's own activity table cannot see. gaEvent (analytics.ts:22-27) adds only `campus`, so there is no persona dimension in GA4 either. Add an anonymous dw_anon_id plus `persona` and `journey_day` to every event, and let track-activity.js accept anon_id when there is no email. Nothing below is measurable until this lands.
journey_entry — detail 'new' | 'returning', fired from the two Yeses on PathAskedOnce. The split the research asks to A/B: 7-day retention, returning framing vs generic.
journey_day_open — detail day number. Opens of the Day N surface, per day. The 40-day drop curve, which no public source will ever supply.
journey_day_read — detail day number. Completion per day. Day-1 completion vs day-2 completion is the whole thesis of this design.

journey_whole_chapter — detail day number. How often anyone taps past the assigned verses. If this is high, the sizing decision was wrong and the default should move; if it is near zero, the chapter default was pure friction.
journey_glossary_tap — detail the term. Proves or kills the literacy scaffold, and tells us which words actually stop people.
journey_question_answered — detail day number. Are the Reflect & Respond questions used, or ignored under the teaching?
journey_connect_tap / journey_connect_dismiss — detail day 10. The relational move: taken, or declined.
journey_return — detail days_since_last. Gives the return curve and the gap-line trigger rate in one event.
comfort_tap_from_journey — how many people on this path reach for comfort, which no one currently knows.
push_unsubscribe — detail persona. The guilt check: if reminder opt-out on this path is above the others, the copy is wounding.
day1_abandon — Read tapped, Mark as read never fired, session ended. The single number that says whether Day 1 is the right size.
Rollup: D1 / D7 / D14 / D30 by persona and by journey_entry, one nightly job. The research's build-first item, scoped to the one path where we already have a natural cohort.
self_serve_levers: TODAY, WITHOUT A DEVELOPER: language (LanguageSwitch on the landing and in the Home header), campus (HomeContextChips 📍 chip — but note it is hidden on this path, so a defaulted new believer cannot set their campus until they change path; that is why the Day 10 connect card has to resolve the campus itself), path (PathSwatch → ChoosePathSheet, one tap saves and opens), and the Sunday QR guest flow (?sunday=1). That is the whole list. Every word of the 40-day journey is a repo file.

LEVER 1 — the campus welcome line. A campus_content row of type 'journey_welcome' per campus, published from /staff exactly the way campus-corner items already are (intake.js action 'submit', read back by campus-content.js). It renders as the one supporting line under the journey hero for readers at that campus, falling back to the shipped pathway_how_it_works line. A campus pastor owns one sentence on the screen their new believers see every day, with no deploy.

LEVER 2 — who receives the Day 10 request. Already self-serve: the receiving pastor is resolved from staff_roster.campus_id, which admin maintains through intake.js roster_save. Adding or changing the person who reaches out is a roster edit, not a code change. (Ashley must still rule WHO that is per campus — it is in his open decisions.)

LEVER 3 — the glossary. A journey_glossary table (term, plain_meaning, lang, active) edited in /staff behind the existing admin-only guard, exactly like intake_questions (question_save / question_delete / question_reorder). Deliberately ADMIN-only, not campus-pastor: a one-line definition of grace or repentance is doctrine in miniature and should not fork by campus. A bundled default in src/data/journey-glossary.ts ships with the app so the row is optional and the feature works offline.

LEVER 4 — reminder copy. push-send.js TEMPLATES are hardcoded arrays; a push_templates table (persona, lang, body, active) read by the cron makes the daily wording admin-editable. Until then, every wording change is a function deploy.

NOT SELF-SERVE, AND HONEST ABOUT IT — the 40 days themselves. Title, theme, lesson, questions and the assigned verses live in books/faith-pathway.json in the repo, in four languages, and any edit there is subject to the service-worker ruling: /books/* must stay network-first with cache as offline fallback only, and CACHE_NAME/STATIC_CACHE plus SW_VERSION bump together for any sw.js change. The smallest lever that changes this: keep the JSON as the shipped default and let an admin-only journey_overrides row (day, field, lang, value) merge over it at load — fill-only, same discipline as applyMisc, so a bad row can never delete a shipped day. That is a build, not a config, and it is Ashley's call whether it is worth it.

ALSO NOT SELF-SERVE: adding or removing a path (PATHS + Persona type + ChoosePathSheet icon map + i18n + PERSONA_CONFIGS), changing sectionOrder, changing the Day 1 landing copy (src/data/day1-landing.ts), and changing when the gates fire (coldStart.ts needsPathAsk, App.tsx wiring).

open_decisions: Day 40. Does the fortieth day get a named ending and one offer of the congregation path (a real choice, source 'upgrade' through the existing sheet)? This is NOT comfort's banned 'Feeling Stronger?' prompt — that ruling is scoped to the comfort path, where nothing may ever be asked. But it is close enough in shape that it needs Ashley's explicit word before anyone builds it.

Who at each campus receives the Day 10 'read with me' request, and what they are expected to do with it. The research names this as his decision. Without a named person per campus the card is a promise the app cannot keep, and it should not ship.

The comfort line on Home. It is designed onto the Day N surface only, because his 1 Sep ruling says every line on the I'm-New home relates to the sage journey button. If he wants it on Home too, it is one muted line under the hero — his call, not a designer's.

The returning greeting. 'Good to have you back, {first}. Pick it up where you are.' changes a line he has seen on the front page for months. If he would rather the two doors stay analytics-only, the split still measures 7-day retention and the greeting stays exactly as it is.

Translated copy sign-off. The new lines (both-doors line, waiting line, whole-chapter toggle, glossary, Day 10 card, comfort line) need es/pt/id or t() prints raw keys. Under his ruling Claude drafts and he approves before ship — he waived review only for the comfort devotions. Does he want to read these, or delegate them the same way?

Anonymous analytics. Sending a dw_anon_id for pre-email readers is the only way to see this persona's retention at all. It must respect dw_cookie_consent. His call whether an anonymous id before consent is acceptable, or whether the events wait for the accept.
risks: This touches the two most owner-preview-gated surfaces in the app: the Superdesign Day 1 landing and the Day N reading surface. PR #80 deleted HomeScreen and ten sections and was reverted the same night with 'what have you done… you have completely stripped. go back.' Nothing here merges without Ashley on a deploy preview saying so. Note also: the repo does not allow auto-merge, and a rebase plus force-push needs about 20 seconds before GitHub reports MERGEABLE.

Verse filtering could break highlights. ScripturePassage builds highlight refs as `${passageRef}:${verseNum}` — the filter must keep the real verse numbers, or a highlight made on the sliced view will not match one made on the whole chapter, and the two views will disagree about the same verse.
Do not touch the fetch. fetchKJV cannot resolve a verse range; a well-meaning 'just fetch the verses' change silently kills the offline KJV fallback and every reader without ESV gets an empty card.

dw_journey_entry is a synced dw_* record. It must be merged into what is currently in localStorage and touch only its own field. Rebuilding a dw_* record from React state is the mistake that destroyed nine completed days in PR #64. It also needs a dw_misc_meta stamp to be newest-wins, or it will behave as fill-only and a later correction will never propagate.
The i18n-keys regression test fails on any key missing a language. Six or seven new keys × four languages, and existing entries use \uXXXX escapes.

Changing the primary button's word touches a store boundary that has bitten before. 'Mark as read' and 'Mark Complete' were once two different actions writing two different stores; the rename must be copy only — savePathwayProgressFromLesson stays the single completion path, and dw_reading_done stays stamped from the local en-CA date.

No /books edit is proposed, so no service-worker bump is needed. If anyone extends this into the JSON, /books/* must stay network-first and CACHE_NAME/STATIC_CACHE plus SW_VERSION bump together — and returning readers only see the change on the SECOND open after deploy.

Push cannot be verified on a deploy preview. pushSupported() allowlists futuresdailyword.com/www/localhost only, so any reminder-copy change is verifiable on prod or localhost, never on the preview Ashley is looking at.

The Day 10 card is a promise from a real church. If no one at the campus is watching the intake queue, a new believer asks for help on day 10 and hears nothing. That is worse than not offering. Ship the card only after the receiving person exists.
Anonymous analytics is a privacy question, not just a plumbing one. It must respect dw_cookie_consent and must never carry anything identifying.

node_modules is not installed locally (Netlify builds it) — a fresh worktree needs its own npm ci. And the main tree regularly carries another session's uncommitted work; do this in an isolated worktree.
